read.bigIdea: A spirit with sugar and flavor added.
read.where: A **liqueur** is a spirit sweetened and flavored. In the EU it has at least **15% ABV** and, for most, at least **100 grams of sugar per liter**. Families on our back bar: **orange** (triple sec, Cointreau, Grand Marnier), **coffee**, **nut**, **herbal** (Chartreuse, Bénédictine), **cream** and **fruit and floral** (elderflower, cassis, maraschino).

read.where: **Amaro** means “bitter” in Italian: herbal liqueurs that are bitter and sweet at once. **Aperitivo** bitters like **Aperol** and **Campari** are lighter and brighter, for before dinner. **Fernet** is one of the most bitter. **Carciofo** amari, like Cynar, use artichoke. **Alpine** amari use mountain herbs.

read.where: **Vermouth** is wine flavored with herbs and spices and fortified with spirit. **Sweet** (red, Italian-style) goes in Manhattans and Negronis; **dry** (pale, French-style) goes in Martinis. It is wine, so once open it fades: keep it in the **fridge** and finish it within **one to three months**.
read.mixup: **Sweet** vermouth for a Manhattan and Negroni. **Dry** vermouth for a Martini.

keyPoints.line: at a time: bitters are strong.

read.bigIdea: A dash seasons the whole drink.
read.where: **Bitters** are strong infusions of herbs, roots and spices, added a **dash** at a time. **Aromatic** bitters (Angostura) go in the Old Fashioned and Manhattan. **Creole** bitters (Peychaud’s) are the Sazerac’s. **Orange** bitters suit Martinis. There are **chocolate**, **mole** and **herbal** bitters too.

facts.fact: A liqueur is a spirit sweetened and flavored. In the EU it has at least 15% ABV and, for most, at least 100 grams of sugar per liter. Families on our back bar: orange (triple sec, Cointreau, Grand Marnier), coffee, nut, herbal (Chartreuse, Bénédictine), cream and fruit and floral (elderflower, cassis, maraschino).
facts.source: EU spirit drinks regulation 2019/787, Annex I (eur-lex.europa.eu)

facts.fact: Amaro means “bitter” in Italian: herbal liqueurs that are bitter and sweet at once. Aperitivo bitters like Aperol and Campari are lighter and brighter, for before dinner. Fernet is one of the most bitter. Carciofo amari, like Cynar, use artichoke. Alpine amari use mountain herbs.

Vermouth is wine flavored with herbs and spices and fortified with spirit. Sweet (red, Italian-style) goes in Manhattans and Negronis; dry (pale, French-style) goes in Martinis. It is wine, so once open it fades: keep it in the fridge and finish it within one to three months.

Bitters are strong infusions of herbs, roots and spices, added a dash at a time. Aromatic bitters (Angostura) go in the Old Fashioned and Manhattan. Creole bitters (Peychaud’s) are the Sazerac’s. Orange bitters suit Martinis. There are chocolate, mole and herbal bitters too.
